# Eigen Energy — Top challenges in solar EPC projects and how to avoid them
URL: https://www.eigen.energy/articles/top-challenges-solar-epc-projects-how-to-avoid-them
Date captured: 2026-08-11

## TL;DR Key takeaways
- Roof constraints can limit system size, layout, structural feasibility.
- Approval delays often from incomplete documents, missing coordination, late submissions.
- Design mistakes reduce generation, increase risk, create rework at installation.
- Project delays when procurement, approvals, site readiness not aligned.
- Poor coordination between owners, consultants, contractors, installers = avoidable friction.
- Best risk reduction: proper site assessment, clear scope, disciplined PM.

## Roof constraints underestimated
Roof space limited by existing equipment, access paths, fire setbacks, shading, weight loading, structural conditions. Usable area may be far less than expected -> affects capacity, layout efficiency, ROI. Structural reinforcement may be required. Avoid via early roof survey, structural review, shading analysis, realistic yield study.

## Approvals can slow projects
Timelines longer than expected; multiple stakeholders: landlord, BMS, authority submissions, utility coordination, internal sign-offs. Delays from incomplete docs, unclear scope, late stakeholders. Mitigate: identify every reviewer at start, document checklist early, approval roadmap from day one.

## Design mistakes create long-term problems
Poor assumptions (roof, cable routing, inverter placement, shading, load balancing) -> underperformance, higher maintenance, rework. Design must reflect actual site, operational constraints, maintenance access. Validate against real site data, not desktop estimates.

## Delays from weak sequencing
Procurement before design finalized; install before approvals; equipment before site ready -> bottlenecks, wasted time/cost. Treat as coordinated chain with milestones/dependencies; regular reviews.

## Poor coordination increases risk
Multiple parties (owners, ops, consultants, engineers, contractors, safety, tenants/FM). Site access issue halts install; design change affects procurement; late operational restriction forces reschedule. Need single point of project ownership for C&I.

## Operations continuity must be protected
C&I solar cannot disrupt business. Warehouses/factories/offices have active operations. Plan site-specific work schedule, access strategy, safety protocol; coordinate around operational hours.

## Commissioning and handover overlooked
Focus on install, less on commissioning/handover = mistake. System incomplete until tested, documented, handed over with procedures, monitoring access, maintenance guidance. Without proper handover, owner struggles to track performance. Provide commissioning records, as-built docs, warranty info, O&M plan.

## FAQ
- EPC = engineering, procurement, construction.
- Delays: approval bottlenecks, incomplete designs, procurement issues, site readiness, poor coordination.
- Biggest challenge: roof feasibility (size, layout, loading, performance).
- Reduce risk: site assessment, right stakeholders early, full-delivery EPC partner.
